agent: Independent Senior Application Security Reviewer, round 4
summary: HEAD matched the requested SHA at start and end; worktree clean. Reviewed the full 164a831..HEAD diff and related authorization/media paths offline. SECR-002 is closed in source: all three realm flow definitions are identical. Cookie and forms are ALTERNATIVE only inside the REQUIRED login subflow; successful cookie authentication completes that subflow, not the outer browser flow. The subsequent CONDITIONAL staff subflow becomes required when the role condition matches, enforcing REQUIRED OTP; customers skip it. This agrees with the maintainer-reported Keycloak 26.8.0 replay, which was not independently executed. CR3-002 is closed in source by scheduling sealed-upload cleanup after ticket expiry plus one minute. The fingerprint delimiter collision is also corrected. SECR-003 is only partially fixed: document rollback deletion is removed, public-image rollback deletion remains. SECR-004 protects files after successful rendering but leaves a first-render exposure window. SECR-001 remains open by decision because enforcement defaults off. With the flag ON, no inspected path gives a password-only token lacking an accepted MFA assertion staff authority: bearer and web authentication use AccountMapper, and scoped authorization checks its authorities. The environment alias is now wired through application.yaml and preview compose. All conclusions from this review are static-only, including concurrency, file-permission timing, cleanup scheduling and authorization behavior. Tests were inspected, not executed. Live realm rollout, deployed configuration, runtime claim issuance, storage behavior and upstream dependency advisories were not verified. No additional concrete vulnerability was established in the diff.

findings.title: Default-off MFA enforcement still permits password-only staff grant holders
findings.scenario: An active account has an application staff grant but lacks the Keycloak matbakhy-staff role. With the default configuration, password-only authentication skips the realm's role-conditioned OTP and receives staff authorities.
findings.expected: Every staff grant holder must assert MFA before using staff authority.
findings.actual: The default-off gate issues database-backed permissions without checking MFA. This is the still-open SECR-001 decision, not a newly introduced bypass.
findings.evidence: AccountMapper.java:33 defaults false and :55-58 conditionally adds permissions. application.yaml:71 binds IDENTITY_REQUIRE_STAFF_MFA with default false; deploy/web-preview/compose.yaml:150 also defaults false. With the flag true, both bearer and web paths use this mapper and cannot obtain these authorities without StaffAssurance.assertsMfa succeeding.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile staff grant holders with the provider MFA policy and enable enforcement in the target environment.
findings.repro_test: Using synthetic accounts, grant support.case to an account without the realm role. Verify password-only access succeeds with the default and is denied with IDENTITY_REQUIRE_STAFF_MFA=true. Static-only; not executed.

findings.title: Public-image rollback callback can still delete a concurrent retry's approved object
findings.scenario: Completion A writes media/<id>.jpg and rolls back. After its database lock releases but before its rollback callback deletes the object, completion B writes the same key and commits approval. A's delayed callback then deletes B's approved image.
findings.expected: Rollback cleanup must not delete an object referenced by a committed approval.
findings.actual: The document branch no longer registers rollback deletion, but the public branch retains unconditional deletion of its shared deterministic key.
findings.evidence: MediaService.java:198-203 writes the deterministic public key and registers deletion. The callback executes after rollback at :305-312, outside the reference-aware cleanup worker. SECR-003 therefore remains open for public variants.
findings.suggested_fix: Use attempt-specific keys with durable reference-aware cleanup, or otherwise remove unconditional rollback deletion of the shared public key.
findings.repro_test: Pause A's rollback callback after database rollback, complete and commit B for the same synthetic media asset, resume A, and assert B's public object remains readable. Static-only; concurrency reproduction not executed.

findings.title: Credential files are written before their parent directory becomes private
findings.scenario: On a fresh render with a traversable deployment parent and a normal 022 umask, mkdir creates traversable generated directories. An unrelated local account opens or copies the rendered credential files before chmod 700 runs. A rendering failure before chmod can leave the exposure persistent.
findings.expected: The output directory must be private before any credential-bearing file is created or truncated.
findings.actual: The script writes both files at lines 62-65 and restricts GENERATED_DIR only at line 68. Successful completion protects subsequent pathname access but cannot revoke a file descriptor already opened during rendering.
findings.evidence: deploy.sh:59-70 has mkdir, credential rendering, then chmod 700 in that order. render establishes no restrictive umask; umask 077 at :30 belongs only to init_secrets. This leaves SECR-004 partially unresolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Create and restrict GENERATED_DIR before writing secrets, and establish restrictive creation permissions before rendering. Apply container-readable file permissions only beneath the already-private parent.
findings.repro_test: Render synthetic credentials under a traversable temporary parent with umask 022, pause before chmod, and attempt reads as an unrelated UID. Also simulate rendering failure before chmod. Reads must fail throughout. Static-only; not executed.
